openQuestions: 1. Should generated pictures be allowed at all? Every article already has a hand-built pictogram plate, and the repository has no written rule about generated imagery. I allowed generation for cover-ink-study (after stock) but did not copy Machines on Machines' ban on generated photorealism. Do you want the same binding rule here (it can be added as an admin), or no generation?

2. The pictogram is a drawn figure type: sources is figure-system only, pointing at publication/pictograms (the registry and art, one metaphor, one accent element, one motion beat, 320 by 320 line art). Is that the right model, given pictograms are React components rendered per slug and there is no figure.json step like Machines on Machines has?

3. 'Ink study' is my name for the look of public/seed-art/theme-ink-study: line drawing on grid paper inside a rounded plate, with one warm accent. It is the closest thing to a generated-picture style in the repository, but it predates the redesign (the accent is brown, the redesign's accent is tomato). Which accent should pictures use, and is the ink study the look you want for generated covers?

4. Smallest card width: 160px for covers and 120px for the social card are placeholders, to be read from the blog index cards. Inline pictograms sit in the body, so 343px is the phone width, taken from Machines on Machines, not from this site.
5. Night pictures. The site has Day and Night themes and pictogram strokes change with the theme. Should a generated cover also have a Night version?

howToSave: The profile is under the 'profile' key: jq .profile threat-intelligence.json > /tmp/ti-profile.json; papyrus images profile diff --file /tmp/ti-profile.json; papyrus images profile save --file /tmp/ti-profile.json --reason '...' --expected-current-version-id none.

identity.summary: Practical and sober: light line art on cool paper, one signal accent in tomato red.
identity.masterPrompt: Line drawing on a flat cool-paper ground. Thin dark strokes, rounded corners, one accent element in the signal colour and nothing else in colour. No gradients, no texture, no photographic lighting.
